What is Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)
•  Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), commonly known as Speech-to-Text (STT),
    is the computational task of mapping an acoustic speech waveform to the
   corresponding string of words.
•   It takes the digitized audio features and translates them into discrete text tokens,
    like letters or words, that a computer or robot can actually process.

   neither understands the meaning of the text nor does it involve
   the robot speaking back to the user (Text-to-Speech, or TTS)
•  While traditional ASR was limited to transcription, modern
    state-of-the-art models are multitask systems that perform
   language identification, speech translation, and voice activity
   detection simultaneously.

Stage 1: Digitization
•   Digitization converts speech(analog) into a machine-understandable format(digital)
•  Involves sampling followed by quantization.
   – Step 1: Sampling converts a continuous analog signal into discrete digital
       values by measuring the signal’s amplitude at regular time intervals.
          • Sampling rate (in Hertz) is the number of total samples taken per second
          during digitization. E.g., 16,000 Hz for microphone speech.
          • To accurately measure a sound wave, the sampling rate must be at least
          twice the frequency of the wave.
          • This maximum measurable frequency is known as

Stage 2: Windowing/Framing
•  Speech is a non-stationary signal, meaning its properties constantly change over
   time as the speaker talks.
•  Since computers need to analyze stable sounds, the system breaks the continuous
   signal into small, roughly stationary time chunks by multiplying the signal by a
   windowing function to extract a frame.
•  This relies on three parameters:
    –  the window size (or frame size in ms)
    –  the frame stride(the shift/offset showing how far the window moves forward each time)
    –  the window shape

concepts.title: ASR output
concepts.description: ASR or speech-to-text produces a textual representation, not an intent or a synthesized voice.

concepts.title: Multitask capability
concepts.description: The slide names possible multitask capabilities without defining every call as a combined output.

concepts.title: Microphone conversion

concepts.title: Digitization placement
concepts.description: The diagram is a conceptual workflow, not a literal placement of the analog-to-digital converter.

concepts.title: Waveform axes
concepts.description: These are comparative waveform cues, not a full psychoacoustic model of arbitrary speech.

concepts.title: Feature pipeline order
concepts.description: The source presents a traditional chain; a modern model may stop at log-Mel features.

concepts.title: Sampling versus quantization
concepts.description: A time-sampled sequence is not necessarily amplitude-quantized until the quantizer is specified.

concepts.title: Samples and quantization codes
concepts.description: Sampling rate determines the sample count; bit depth independently determines the amplitude-code count.

concepts.title: Nyquist frequency
concepts.description: The Nyquist boundary is f_s/2; reliable reconstruction also needs appropriate bandlimiting.

concepts.title: Exact Nyquist boundary
concepts.description: At the exact Nyquist boundary, phase matters. The usual safe reconstruction statement uses a bandlimited spectrum strictly below half the sample rate.

concepts.title: Short-time stationarity
concepts.description: Local stationarity makes a per-frame spectral summary useful without assuming the entire utterance is stationary.

concepts.title: Complete-frame count
concepts.description: The final start must satisfy start + 400 ≤ 16000.

concepts.title: Window operation
concepts.description: A window weights the selected samples without summing across indices in this equation.

concepts.title: Rectangular window
concepts.description: The rectangular window performs hard selection without tapering its interior weights.

concepts.title: Hamming endpoint conflict
concepts.description: The periodic formula is meaningful, but its first weight is nonzero. It must not be silently replaced by a Hann window.

concepts.title: Periodic and symmetric Hamming
concepts.description: Do not label the printed denominator L as erroneous merely because a symmetric implementation uses L−1.

concepts.title: Taper purpose
concepts.description: The taper changes the analysis window; it does not recover frequencies with unlimited resolution.

concepts.title: DFT versus FFT
concepts.description: An algorithmic speedup should not be confused with a different mathematical transform.

concepts.title: Four-point DFT
concepts.description: The sign convention and normalization are part of the transform definition.

concepts.title: DFT frequency bins
concepts.description: The frame length and sampling rate determine the frequency grid.

concepts.title: Complex spectrum versus power
concepts.description: The complex coefficient is not itself a scalar energy; squared magnitude gives the corresponding unnormalized spectral-power value.

concepts.title: Mel filter-bank diagram
concepts.description: The Mel mapping allocates finer physical-frequency resolution to the lower-frequency region.

concepts.title: Mel conversion
concepts.description: The printed formula uses the natural logarithm and the stated constants.

concepts.title: Inverse Mel mapping
concepts.description: The inverse must map m = 0 to f = 0.

concepts.title: Filter-channel energies
concepts.description: A filter bank changes the spectral-bin vector into one energy per channel.

concepts.title: Logarithm at zero energy
concepts.description: The generic elementwise-log diagram omits numerical stabilization details.

concepts.title: Generic log-Mel versus exact preprocessing
concepts.description: The checked OpenAI implementation uses a floor, log10, a dynamic-range bound and rescaling; do not silently equate it with the generic lecture vector.

concepts.title: MFCC purpose
concepts.description: MFCC features summarize acoustic structure rather than replacing language decoding.

concepts.title: Static versus dynamic features
concepts.description: Energy and dynamic features depend on the chosen feature configuration, not merely the name MFCC.

concepts.title: Modern feature endpoint
concepts.description: The pipeline diagram is not a universal requirement for every recognition architecture.

concepts.title: Traditional ASR components
concepts.description: The search decoder combines acoustic, pronunciation and language information to select hypotheses.

concepts.title: Independent training qualification
concepts.description: End-to-end integration changes modeling boundaries but does not make preprocessing or decoding disappear.

concepts.title: Audio-text sequence mismatch

concepts.title: ASR intersection diagram

concepts.title: One-frame CNN

concepts.title: Temporal cross-correlation

concepts.title: Stride and output length
concepts.description: The output length depends jointly on kernel, padding and stride.

concepts.title: Multiple input channels

concepts.title: Subsampling and alignment
